subject: Discovery recap: data privacy & logging requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finup.com>, security@finup.com
Cc: 
Date: 2026-08-23T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: data privacy & logging requirements

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from my side and a proposed set of next steps so we can align with your security and procurement teams. Please reply with any corrections.

Pain points you shared:
- Need strict controls around PII in logs and generated outputs (account numbers, SSNs, full names).
- Current inference stack is a managed LLM endpoint (vendor X) but you're seeing high egress/retention costs and limited auditability.
- Security team requires immutable audit trails and tamper-evident logs for regulatory review.

Goals / success criteria:
- No raw PII stored beyond X hours (you mentioned 90 days as a target).
- Audit logs that show who queried what and when, with exportable, signed records retained for 2 years.
- Ability to redact or obfuscate PII at ingestion and to perform selective deletions on request.
- Performance SLA to support peak inference throughput for fraud-detection flows.

Current stack (what I heard): vendor X endpoints + internal proxy; data plane currently in us-west; tokens routed through a 3rd-party enrichment service.

Open questions / clarifications we need from you:
1) Confirm the retention window target (you mentioned 90 days; is that firm or negotiable?)
2) Are there any regulatory constraints (PCI, GLBA, HIPAA) that apply to the workloads we discussed?
3) Who on your side will own the technical security review? (Name and email)

Next steps (proposed):
- I'll share a one-page SOC 2 summary and a Mutual Action Plan (attached) for your legal/procurement review. (Attaching redwood_soc2_summary.pdf and MAP_FinUp.xlsx)
- Schedule a technical security review with our Security/Compliance engineer (suggest Aug 30 or Sep 1).
- Provide a short doc with any mandatory retention or redaction rules to validate feasibility.

If that all looks right, I'll loop in our security lead and rachel from Ops to start the artifact exchange.

Thanks — talk soon.


Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments referenced: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf, MAP_FinUp.xlsx

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finup.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@finup.com
Date: 2026-08-23T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: data privacy & logging requirements

Thanks Marissa — great summary and aligned on most points. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Retention: 90 days for raw inputs is our target for now. We may ask for longer retention of metadata/audit logs (up to 2 years) for compliance audits.
- Redaction: We need the ability to auto-redact PII at ingestion (patterns: SSN, credit card, account numbers, emails) and an admin path to manually request purges.
- Audit logs: Must include user id, request id, model version, timestamp, and a signed checksum (we can provide format).

Regulatory: Not PCI or HIPAA for this initial use case, but GLBA-ish controls are required because of financial identifiers.

Technical owner for the security review: Priya Natarajan (priya.n@finup.com) — she's on security and will join the review. Procurement timeline: aiming to finalize commercial terms by mid-September.

We're good with your proposed next steps. Please send over the SOC2 summary and MAP and we'll get Priya and procurement involved. Also please confirm whether redaction can be performed at the edge (before data is persisted) vs post-hoc.

Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Integrations, FinUp Corp
alex.turner@finup.com
+1 (212) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com, dev.patel@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finup.com>, priya.n@finup.com
Date: 2026-08-24T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap: data privacy & logging requirements — SOC2/MAP attached

Rachel / Dev — looping you both in to start the artifact exchange and to scope redaction/retention feasibility. See thread below from Alex. I attached the SOC2 one-pager and a proposed Mutual Action Plan for FinUp.

Key asks from FinUp: 
- 90-day retention for raw inputs; 2-year retention for audit logs (signed checksums).
- Auto-redaction at ingestion for defined PII patterns + admin manual purge capability.
- Exportable, tamper-evident audit logs with user+request+model metadata.

Initial asks for our side: 
- Can we confirm we support ingestion-time redaction? If not fully, can we offer an ingestion pipeline that flags and strips PII before persistence?
- What are the operational impacts to performance and cost (rough ballpark)?
- Which SOC2 artifacts can we share publicly vs NDA-only?

Attachments: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (public summary), MAP_FinUp.xlsx (internal MAP, will share DocuSign link once updated).

Proposed internal owners: Rachel — procurement/commercial; Dev — security/compliance engineer to lead the technical review.

I'll schedule a 60-min tech review for Aug 30 10:00am PT unless you prefer another slot.


Marissa

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finup.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com
Cc: priya.n@finup.com, security@finup.com
Date: 2026-08-24T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: data privacy & logging requirements — SOC2/MAP attached

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Aug 30 at 10:00am PT works for Priya and me. A couple quick confirmations before the technical review: 

1) Please confirm whether redaction is available at ingestion (pre-persistence) as a standard capability or whether we'll need to route through a preprocessing step. If ingestion redaction is possible, can you share supported pattern types (regex, entity-based) and whether custom rules are supported?
2) Can you confirm audit-log retention options and whether we can export signed, downloadable logs for audits?

If you can send short answers to those two items ahead of the review, that'll help Priya prep. After the review, we'll expect a short feasibility note and any recommended config changes (batching, caching, or quantization choices) that impact retention or auditability.

See you Aug 30.

Best,
Alex
